open_points.subject: A8 ServiceExit classification after listening
open_points.text: SERVED, value `served`: after it has served, the web server returns because a SIGINT or SIGTERM stopped it; and SERVER_FAILED, value `server_failed`: after it has served, the process ends in any other way.
open_points.question: Which outcome takes precedence when SIGINT or SIGTERM causes the web server to return but the process then ends because shutdown or cleanup fails, or when a server failure and the signal occur concurrently; and what observable condition proves that the server returned because of the signal?
options: SERVED whenever SIGINT or SIGTERM initiated the server return, regardless of a later shutdown failure
SERVER_FAILED whenever the final process termination is unsuccessful, even after a signal-initiated server return
Use an explicit precedence rule based on which event was recorded first
open_points.default_guess: Classify by the final termination: SERVED only when signal-initiated shutdown completes successfully; otherwise SERVER_FAILED.

witness.initial: The web server has begun listening.
events: The web server returns in response to SIGTERM.
A shutdown or cleanup step raises an error and the process exits.
outcomes: SERVED with status 0 because the web server returned because SIGTERM stopped it.
SERVER_FAILED with status 1 because the process ultimately ended through a shutdown failure.
witness.observer: The process supervisor and any caller or test observing the ServiceExit outcome

open_points.subject: A8 EXIT_STATUSES for signal termination
open_points.text:
START_FAILED, value `start_failed`: the process ends before it listens, whatever ends it, a signal included;

| `START_FAILED` | 1 |
open_points.question: Does “a signal included” include signals that the process cannot handle or convert into status 1, and if so, what component must translate signal termination into the declared exit status?
options: Only handled signals are classified through ServiceExit; unhandled or uncatchable signals retain native signal termination status
A parent or launcher must translate every pre-listening signal termination to status 1
The statement applies to the semantic outcome only, while the operating-system exit status may differ from EXIT_STATUSES
open_points.default_guess: Apply EXIT_STATUSES only when the service controls its return; unhandled or uncatchable signals retain their native termination status.

witness.initial: The service process is starting and has not begun listening.
events: An operator or supervisor sends SIGKILL to the service process.
outcomes: The termination is START_FAILED and is reported as status 1 because every signal is included.
The process retains native signal termination status because it cannot execute the EXIT_STATUSES mapping.
witness.observer: The process supervisor or deployment system observing the process exit status
